Title: Cyber and drone incidents point to a more unstable world
Article:
AS multiple computer systems crashed around the world last week and unidentified drones piled pressure on US air bases in Britain, Southeast Asian nations firmed up plans to build and share oil supplies in the event of a major crisis.
Their move was overshadowed by the run-up to Thursday's talks between the leaders of the United States, China and Russia — Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin — in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.
It was a meeting that gave the White House a chance to demonstrate its power and reach despite the loss of both houses of Congress to the Democrats.
But as the Asian energy security effort shows, for countries watching from the sidelines, the focus is increasingly on a host of fast-growing risks that they may need to manage with much less leadership from Washington.
This year has delivered such a range of shocks – some direct from the White House, others from new dynamics including the rise of AI – that a range of governments are gradually but radically adjusting their world view.
"The world has changed," Australian Secretary to the Treasury Jenny Wilkinson told the Economic Security Forum in Sydney this month, pointing to "intensifying geopolitical competition and a more volatile and fragmented international environment."
Another speaker, Marco Buti, former director general for economic and financial affairs at the European Commission, used the phrase "predatory superpowers" to refer to Washington, Moscow and Beijing.
[[nid:1582325]]
While all three capitals reject the characterisation, the United States, Russia and China are delivering disruption that other powers must learn to manage.
OpenAI executive Dean Ball described in an essay what he called a growing "silent consensus" in Silicon Valley that increased algorithmic decision-making was now on the brink of taking over.
"Taken together, the decisions could produce a world in which people have forfeited effective authority over much of our civilisation," he wrote, adding that this was becoming increasingly privately widespread among the tech elite.
Traditional US allies like to think they have a plan, at least to deal with growing conflict risks: deepening coordination with the Pentagon.
But, in Nato, Asia and the Middle East there is growing coordination with the US Project Maven AI-enabled command and control system, officials have expressed concern that in a crisis they might be denied access to US AI or satellites.
Coupled with that is nervousness that the US may no longer have a handle on key events.
Disruption to US air traffic control and key Microsoft systems as well as details of the use in China of cutting-edge AI chips from tech firm Nvidia have only fuelled those fears.
Questions remain over the exact causes of last week's 24-hour blackout of key Microsoft services including email programme Outlook on which many companies and governments depend, as well as the failure of US air traffic control systems.
The unidentified drone activity at a US air base in Britain last week came after bombers used to strike Iran were moved out of Britain following the arrest of five men near another base.
Other nations report unauthorised and unidentified drone activity near major bases include Australia in August.
[[nid:1582324]]
On Tuesday, Norway's oil and gas company Equinor reported that it was under an ongoing cyberattack, declining to give more details.
Google's Threat Intelligence Group also warned that a new era of "autonomous attacks" in cyberspace had now arrived, with hackers able to delegate much of their work to AI agents that probe relentlessly for vulnerabilities without human input.
Drones are also in much more plentiful supply, with skills and technologies built amid fighting in Ukraine increasingly for sale to those with the ability to pay.
Considerable risks remain, however, particularly if hostile nations choose to rip up international rules.
One recent private wargame in Singapore suggested a couple of cargo ships carrying autonomous attack drones would be enough to bring that territory to its knees, perhaps as part of a potential larger conflict.
Chinese naval activity around Taiwan has been high as Xi, Putin and Trump approached their meeting, with Beijing also extending its ban on rare-earth exports until the end of January.
So-called "middle powers" have clearly found the Trump-Xi-Putin meeting optics unsettling.
They may find they have to do much more to regain their agency in a world now shifting in strange and complex ways.
* The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar chips in RM10,000 for young racer's world title bid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has donated RM10,000 to young Pahang racer Muhammad Qaish Isyraf Mohd Qayyum to support his campaign at the FIM MotoMini World Final Series in Valencia, Spain.
Anwar's political secretary Datuk Ahmad Farhan Fauzi said the contribution was handed over to the 13-year-old from Indera Mahkota, Kuantan, through his representative yesterday.
In a Facebook post, Ahmad Farhan said Muhammad Qaish Isyraf would compete in the 160cc category at the international championship.
"We hope this contribution will encourage him and help defray some of his expenses while competing in the prestigious championship.
"I also took the opportunity to speak to Qaish via video call to find out how preparations for the championship were progressing," he said.
He said the initiative reflected the Madani government's commitment to recognising and supporting local talent by providing opportunities for young Malaysians to develop their potential and make the country proud on the international stage.

Title: 12,471 raids, 46,426 arrests: Immigration turns up heat
Article:
KLANG: A total of 46,426 illegal immigrants were detained in 12,471 enforcement operations conducted nationwide by the Immigration Department from January to date.
Its deputy director-general (Operations), Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli, said the operations also saw 161,748 people screened and more than 2,000 employers taken to task.
"This shows how seriously we take enforcement. More than 37 operations are conducted daily on average. Not an hour goes by without an operation, and we will not compromise with any foreign national who commits an offence.
"Action has also been taken against more than 2,000 employers, while 52,743 foreigners have been deported to their countries of origin," he told reporters after joining Op Sasar at a factory in Meru here today.
He said the integrated operations involved the Labour Department, National Registration Department (NRD), Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) and local authorities.
He said enforcement efforts targeted not only foreign workers but also employers and other parties who facilitated immigration offences.
Operations would continue to detect, arrest, prosecute and deport foreigners who violated the Immigration Act 1959/63, Passports Act 1966, Immigration Regulations 1963 and Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007.
Earlier, Lokman Effendi, accompanied by Immigration Department Enforcement Division director Datuk Basri Othman, joined Op Sasar at a nail manufacturing factory in Meru at 6pm.
The operation, conducted with the Department of Labour Peninsular Malaysia, screened 131 male foreigners, resulting in the detention of 71.
Those detained comprised 51 Bangladeshis, 19 Nepalese and a Taiwanese national for offences including overstaying, misusing passes and failing to produce valid identification documents.
The operation also uncovered unhygienic and poorly maintained conditions, including overcrowded workers' quarters that failed to meet safety requirements.
All detainees were taken to an immigration detention depot for further action.
Meanwhile, Lokman Effendi said 1,702 foreigners had been screened at 34 factories nationwide since Wednesday, resulting in 519 arrests and 42 witness summonses issued to employers and premises owners.
The Department of Labour Peninsular Malaysia is investigating the cases under the Employees' Minimum Standards of Housing, Accommodations and Amenities Act 1990 (Act 446) and the Employment Act 1955.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'No pathway to urgent care': MSF warns of fallout from UNHCR move
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Refugees and asylum-seekers in Malaysia risk losing access to life-saving healthcare and protection following the abrupt suspension of UNHCR registration.
Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF), commonly known as Doctors With Borders, said the move could force vulnerable refugees to delay or forgo treatment because of a lack of documentation, fear of arrest and higher medical costs.
The medical humanitarian organisation said the consequences were already being felt, with one patient's sight-saving surgery halted less than a day after the announcement, while others risked permanent disability without orthopaedic treatment.
MSF Malaysia medical coordinator Tetyana Pylypenko said 43 refugees without UNHCR registration had been denied treatment at public healthcare facilities in the past 10 months, even when they or MSF were prepared to pay.
"For medically vulnerable refugees, there is no longer a pathway to urgent care.
"Since 2024, MSF has supported 1,275 of them. Without registration, refugees are likely to delay or avoid seeking care because they lack documentation, fear arrest and face much higher costs.
"When people delay care, they tend to arrive later and sicker, which puts more pressure on emergency departments," she said in a statement today.
MSF was responding to UNHCR Malaysia's announcement on Nov 18 that it had
ceased all refugee registration and documentation activities
, in line with the government's plan to introduce its own registration system.
The organisation said the abrupt transition could have life-threatening consequences, particularly for children, pregnant women and those with chronic or infectious diseases.
It said the UNHCR card had served as a crucial document for refugees, particularly Rohingya, who had been stripped of their citizenship in Myanmar in 1982.
Although offering limited protection, the card allows refugees to access public hospitals at half the foreigner rate and reduces their risk of arbitrary and prolonged detention during raids and roadblocks.
MSF said obtaining the card was already a lengthy process, with some applicants waiting years between registration and an appointment.
It called on the government to ensure the proposed Dokumen Pendaftaran Pelarian (DPP) system provides timely access to healthcare and essential services, alongside safeguards against harm.
The organisation also called for protection to be extended to all refugees and asylum-seekers, including those who are unregistered, awaiting registration or held at immigration detention centres.
"People fleeing persecution should not be treated as criminals," MSF said, calling on the government to clarify the interim safeguards that would apply during the transition.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: The airport debate that Kota Kinabalu cannot dodge
Article:
THERE   has been much debate lately as to whether Kota Kinabalu should have a new airport.
This comes as the current Kota Kinabalu International Airport (KKIA) —  already the second busiest airport in the country — appears to be bursting at the seams despite regular  upgrades,  including a planned RM442.3 million expansion.
There was even a forum recently on "The Future of Kota Kinabalu International Airport: Retain, Expand or Relocate?"
Any visitor to the Sabah capital will surely say retain and expand the existing KKIA based solely on sheer convenience.
The airport juts out to sea at one end  and it  takes less than 15 minutes to get there from the city centre.
But, of course, proximity to the city is a boon and also a bane for KKIA. There is only limited space available for expansion, including a second runway.
Is it feasible to expand seawards, and at what cost? In the final analysis, perhaps the inevitable verdict will be to have a new international airport further out from the city while retaining the existing KKIA as a city airport, much like Subang Airport is for Kuala Lumpur.
Chartered Institute of Logistics and Transport Malaysia Sabah Section deputy chairman Mohd Faizal Malik has called for the state to look beyond the planned expansion of KKIA and assess its long-term capacity needs in support of future aviation growth.
He said increasing its passenger handling capacity from nine million to 12 million annually would not necessarily address the airport's wider operational limitations.
Former Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia chief executive officer Datuk Captain Chester Voo added his voice to the call for an assessment of a potential new airport site, citing the risk of relying on a single runway for an increasingly busy airport.
And  undeniably, at the back of anyone's mind must be the potential high costs involved in building a new airport.
It will likely take billions  to plan and build a new KKIA.
The good news is that much of that spending will probably be well into the future, although seed investments may need to be made immediately in the interest of forward planning.
It will certainly be a more feasible idea than Sarawak's plan to build a new international airport in Kuching, reportedly costing RM100 billion (although that is likely just a projection and includes a new deep-sea port, among other things, at Tanjung Embang, outside Kuching).
Kuching's air traffic movement currently pales in comparison to KKIA's.
Moreover, KKIA is already a busy and viable airport hub and there is still room for expansion where it is, while Kuching needs a lot more work and investment if its airport is to become another hub, along the lines of Doha's airport in Qatar, as Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg has let it be known.
Hence the setting up of AirBorneo, Sarawak's answer to Qatar Airways, the oil-rich emirate's expensive twin investment which took 10 years to  turn a profit but made  Doha a new airport hub.
* The writer views developments in the nation, region and the wider world from his vantage point in Kuching
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's message at Apec meeting goes beyond free trade
Article:
SHENZHEN and Kuala Lumpur both owe their names to water. Shenzhen means "deep channel", after the irrigation channels that once ran through its farmland. Kuala Lumpur is the "muddy confluence" where the Klang and Gombak rivers meet. Both cities grew through the flow of commerce and people.
Few places owe more to integration with the world economy than Shenzhen, which grew in four decades from a border town in Hong Kong's shadow into a city whose economy is now larger than its neighbour's.
Yet, as Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim pointed out at the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) CEO Summit in Shenzhen this week, the conditions that made its rise possible can no longer be taken for granted.
The Apec Policy Support Unit expects the region to grow by 3.4 per cent this year, but its latest figures show that trade remedies and trade-restrictive measures in force outnumber trade facilitating ones by nearly three to one. Technology and critical minerals are increasingly used as instruments of strategic competition.
President Xi Jinping spoke of widening access to China's market and lowering barriers to commerce. Russian President Vladimir Putin warned of a fragmenting world economy. The United States continues to rely on tariffs and controls on advanced technology. Each major power has its own idea of openness, shaped by its strengths and interests.
Then there was the trilateral meeting among Xi, Putin and US President Donald Trump, which some commentators have compared to the Yalta conference of 1945, where US president Franklin D. Roosevelt, British prime minister Winston Churchill and Soviet Union premier Joseph Stalin shaped postwar Europe.
The comparison is imperfect, and the suggestion about it being the harbinger of a new triumvirate world order is far-fetched, but the anxiety behind it is understandable. Great powers should talk to one another, and on matters of war and peace they must.
Still, it is not easy to shake off the notion about the strong doing what they can and the weak having to suffer what they must. Hence, what troubles smaller countries is the lingering suspicion that the powerful may decide the fate of others without those others having a say.
Anwar's keynote at the CEO Summit had already spoken to that concern in his exhortation against letting the region's future "to be dictated by competing spheres of influence, exclusive economic blocs, or the rivalries of great powers". Small countries and emerging economies must be treated with respect, dignity and equality. Every country, whatever its size, should retain the freedom to chart its own course.
For Malaysia, that is the practical meaning of active non-alignment: constructive relations with every major power, and the right to make our own choices.
His larger theme was "equitable openness". The usual measures of openness are tariffs and market access. They still matter, and Malaysia's  growth has depended heavily on trade and foreign investment. But removing barriers does not give every economy the same chance. A country can enjoy access to markets and still depend on technology and capital controlled elsewhere. Anwar's answer was to broaden openness to include the capabilities and policy space that let economies move up the value chain.
At the Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting, Anwar invoked the Confucian ideal of "harmony without uniformity", defended the rules-based multilateral trading system and called for an ethics-driven approach to artificial intelligence and cybersecurity, warning that a breach in one economy is a vulnerability for all. He also called for the benefits of the region's prosperity to extend to the developing economies of the Global South.
Apec brings together 21 economies, including all three major powers, but its decisions are reached by consensus and its commitments are voluntary. Agreement on principles comes far more easily than agreement on hard choices.
Its value also lies in less glamorous work such as paperless trade and modernised customs procedures, which lack the drama of great-power summitry but can lower costs for business.
For Malaysia, neither retreat from the world economy nor dependence on a single power is an answer. Our interests require markets and investment from many partners, and the freedom to decide according to our own circumstances.
Shenzhen and Kuala Lumpur were built on the flow of water, and later, the flow of trade. But the channels of commerce should not serve only those who control them. That, in the end, was the prime minister's argument.
Openness is no longer only about tariffs and market access. It is also about who owns the technology, who controls the supply chains and who is left behind. For a trading nation like Malaysia, the real question is on whose terms the world stays open.
* The writer is executive chairman of the Institute of Strategic and International Studies, Malaysia
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: From old sewing room to podcast studio: School gets digital upgrade
Article:
LENGGONG: More than 620 students, teachers and support staff at SMK Dato' Ahmad here will benefit from improved teaching and digital learning facilities under the government's Sekolah Angkat Madani programme.
The upgrades, carried out by Malaysian Resources Corporation Berhad (MRCB), include a refurbished teachers' room and a dedicated digital learning space.
Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad officially launched the facilities today.
The project benefits 554 students, 58 teachers and nine support staff.
Saarani said collaboration between the government and corporate sector was vital to improving educational facilities.
"On behalf of the Perak government, I would like to thank Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for introducing the Sekolah Angkat Madani programme, which brings together the government and corporate sector to support educational development nationwide.
"I also thank MRCB for upgrading the facilities at SMK Dato' Ahmad.
"These improvements provide teachers and students with a more conducive environment for teaching and learning, an important step towards raising the quality of education in Perak," he said.
The refurbished teachers' room features improved workstations, discussion and meeting areas, new furniture, air-conditioning, lighting and electrical fittings.
A former sewing room and temporary prayer room has also been converted into a digital learning space equipped with interactive smart televisions and a podcast studio.
The studio comes with cameras, lighting, audio systems and recording equipment to help students develop digital literacy, creativity, communication and content creation skills.
MRCB group managing director Datuk Imran Salim said the initiative reflected the company's commitment to supporting communities where it operates.
"As we work closely with the Perak government on major developments such as Ipoh Sentral, it is equally important for us to give back to the communities in which we operate.
"At SMK Dato' Ahmad, we saw an opportunity to contribute not only our resources but also the skills and expertise of our people," he said.
Imran said MRCB's engineering and project management teams were directly involved in ensuring the upgrades met the school's needs.
"We hope these facilities will serve teachers and students well for many years to come," he added.
SMK Dato' Ahmad is one of five schools adopted by MRCB under the programme, which covers two secondary schools and three primary schools in Perak, Penang and Perlis.
Led by the Finance Ministry, the Sekolah Angkat Madani programme brings together government-linked companies, government-linked investment companies and private firms to support educational development nationwide.
After involving 1,000 schools under Phase 1.0, the programme aims to reach 1,500 schools under Phase 2.0.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: Critical hospital failures demand urgent repairs, not another budget cycle
Article:
A MOBILE phone is not emergency lighting and must never become a hospital's last line of defence.
Wangsa Maju member of parliament Zahir Hassan told the Dewan Rakyat that a doctor in Sabah stitched a patient by mobile flashlight.
Power had reportedly failed during surgery. The Health Ministry must establish what happened. Did backup systems work? Was the patient harmed? Checks elsewhere must begin now.
Patient safety cannot wait for an investigation to end. The Malaysian Medical Association has called for an immediate nationwide audit of critical hospital infrastructure.
Its concerns include reported power and water disruptions, backup failures and repeated air conditioning breakdowns. These are not mere maintenance complaints. They demand urgent action.
Start with operating theatres, Intensive Care Units and delivery rooms. Within 30 days, require every hospital to disclose its latest generator, backup battery and emergency lighting tests.
State what equipment those systems actually powered. A test date alone proves nothing. Engineers and clinical teams must verify performance under controlled power failure conditions.
Check water reserves, ventilation, logistics and oxygen supplies. Every critical failure must trigger immediate safeguards. Stop procedures that cannot continue safely. Arrange safe transfers to facilities with confirmed capacity. Resume affected services only after repairs and safety verifications.
An audit is not a repair. A report does not protect patients. The Treasury must reserve funds for urgent replacements and preventive maintenance.
Prioritise hospitals where failure would leave patients without a nearby alternative. Essential repairs cannot wait for another budget cycle.
Give every repair a deadline and an accountable official. Require independent verification before declaring completion. Missed deadlines must trigger escalation and corrective action. Report to Parliament every quarter. Name the failures, completed repairs, missed deadlines and unresolved risks.
Protect staff who report faults and near misses. Investigate any perceived retaliation and hold those responsible accountable.
The Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Sarawak, in September claimed five lives. The ministry told Parliament that the service's suspension affects 85 localities. Sixteen have no alternative access by land or water.
The crash and the hospital outage are separate events. Both raise an urgent question. What happens when a service patients depend on becomes unavailable?
For every remote community, designate an emergency contact, a receiving hospital and transport. Arrange air transport where roads and rivers offer no access. Equip rural clinics to stabilise patients. Rehearse transfers with the teams responsible.
A patient's postcode must never decide their safety. Authorities must fund the repairs, test the backups and answer for failures. Patients cannot be asked to survive on assurances.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saudi Arabia once banned Grand Theft Auto. Now it has a stake in it
Article:
SAUDI ARABIA: Grand Theft Auto, banned in Saudi Arabia until last year, is now being embraced not only by its gamers — a category that includes Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman — but also by its sovereign wealth fund, which the prince chairs.
This week, gamers in Saudi Arabia joined legions of fans around the world to play Grand Theft Auto VI upon its launch — the first new release in the top-selling series since a Saudi ban was scrapped in 2025.
"Playing GTA VI in Saudi Arabia legally makes me so happy, because we're talking about a game that was banned," local content creator Thamer al Dairem said from a windowless, air-conditioned room, lit mostly by the bank of monitors displaying the game.
"We're talking about the biggest game in the world."
Support for and investment in gaming by Saudi Arabia have been rising fast, not least from de facto ruler Mohammed bin Salman, often known by his initials MBS, who told Fox News in 2023 that gaming helped him disconnect and let off steam.
The Public Investment Fund (PIF), the sovereign wealth fund he chairs, owns a major stake worth more than US$2 billion in Take-Two Interactive, the US firm that owns Grand Theft Auto developer Rockstar Games, LSEG Workspace data show.
Changing customs in conservative Saudi Arabia
In August, a consortium including PIF acquired gaming giant Electronic Arts for US$55 billion. This month, gaming software provider Unity Software held talks with investors, including the Saudi sovereign wealth fund, on a potential buyout valuing it at around US$25 billion.
PIF, which has spent the past year consolidating its gaming holdings into a subsidiary, Savvy Games Group, declined to comment.
MBS has been leading a campaign to open Saudi Arabia up and ease strict social and cultural norms rooted in a conservative interpretation of Islam — a far cry from GTA VI's Vice City.
[[nid:1582245]]
GTA VI advertisements have been appearing in some of Saudi Arabia's most popular shopping malls. One image shows the heroine wearing shorts and a crop top, her arm resting on her partner's shoulder — unthinkable a few years ago, when women were required to dress modestly and cover their hair.
MBS's wider reform plan, dubbed Vision 2030, is aimed at reducing reliance on oil and gas revenues, both in the economy and in state revenues, and PIF's strategy is part of that.
"(It) is part of a diversified long-term investment strategy to capture value from industries it does not traditionally operate within," said Piers Harding-Rolls, who researches games at Ampere Analysis.
In Riyadh, al Dairem is now streaming Grand Theft Auto content and says that, while some depictions of violence, drugs and sex are extreme, the game is age-restricted and reflects another country.
"The city is Vice City, and it's representing Miami and the chaotic things that happen. For us Saudis, like, we know that it has nothing to do with us."
The gaming experience, on the other hand, matters hugely to him.
"When I saw the ads of GTA VI in the malls, I was so happy. If you'd asked me if I was ever going to see this, like, 10 years ago in Saudi, I wouldn't have believed it."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: French ex-PM Villepin announces presidential run
Article:
PARIS: France's former prime minister and foreign minister Dominique de Villepin, famed abroad for his excoriating 2003 denunciation of US plans to invade Iraq, said on Friday he was running for president.
Villepin enters an already crowded field of candidates seeking to succeed President Emmanuel Macron, with polls pointing towards a possible run-off between frontrunner Marine Le Pen of the far-right National Rally (RN) and hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) veteran Jean-Luc Melenchon.
Polls so far project Villepin, who has formed his own political party, Humanist France, to win only a low single-digit percentage of votes.
But the former diplomat insisted he was the one to bring about change.
"I am a candidate in the 2027 presidential elections," said the 73-year-old, vowing to end "this decay of France, this spirit of defeat ... that is taking hold of us".
Villepin lashed out at the RN and LFI as "the two major forces of radicalism" who "have increasingly hijacked political life" in France.
But he also took aim at Macron, whom he described as a "phantom president", with his administration ending its second term as a "zombie authority incapable of answering our compatriots".
Villepin, who served as foreign minister from 2002 to 2004 and prime minister from 2005 to 2007 under the presidency of the late right-winger Jacques Chirac, said: "Macronism has opened the path" towards the RN and LFI taking power.
Crowded field
Villepin's impact on the race is so far unclear.
But in a tight contest under a two-round system, every single percentage point in the first round may be crucial for the ultimate outcome.
Fellow former premiers Edouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal are already campaigning, Cannes mayor David Lisnard has seen his ratings climb, while Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner unexpectedly entered the race last week.
This has led to fears that too many candidates on the centre and right in the first round could see them all eliminate themselves and prompt a final clash between Melenchon and Le Pen.
An Ifop-Fiducial poll published on Friday showed Le Pen still well ahead in the first round on 37 per cent, but said Philippe could squeeze into the run-off against her on 19 per cent, ahead of Melenchon — but only if he were the only candidate on the right and centre.
Uphill struggle
Like other candidates, Villepin's first hurdle will be securing the 500 endorsements from elected officials required to run for the presidency.
His team says it has secured about 300 pledges so far.
His previous tilt at the presidency in 2012 floundered at this obstacle when he failed to muster sufficient signatures to stand.
As foreign minister, Villepin won global renown for his eloquent and scathing speech at the United Nations Security Council in February 2003 on plans for war as the United States prepared to invade Saddam Hussein's Iraq over its alleged weapons of mass destruction.
Calling on the international community to "prioritise disarmament in the pursuit of peace", Villepin famously said in a swipe at the United States "that it is an old country — France — from an old continent — Europe — that speaks to you today".
Villepin, for many a living embodiment of a bygone era of "chiraquie" under the former president, who died in 2019, has himself never held elected office.
Key proposals in his manifesto include reducing France's gigantic debt pile and holding more referendums on key issues.
While his past was firmly on the right, aides see a move to the centre and even left.
Asked where he stood, Villepin declined to plunge into this "political quagmire" and said he does not have a "partisan mindset".
He has grown close to former LFI lawmaker Francois Ruffin, while the mutual dislike between Villepin and Chirac's right-wing successor Nicolas Sarkozy — who the former premier is said to disparage as "the dwarf" — has long been an open secret.
For now, polls suggest he would receive between one and three per cent of the vote, although Villepin's vocal condemnation of Israel's war on Gaza and Palestinian fighters group Hamas won some echo among young voters and admiration on the left.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri power struggle: BN, PN assemblymen hold crisis talks
Article:
SEREMBAN: Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) assemblymen are reportedly meeting at Wisma Umno here tonight as the political crisis in Negri Sembilan continues.
The meeting is believed to be linked to the reported consent of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, for Datuk Ismail Lasim
to remain as Menteri Besar.
Among those seen arriving were BN deputy chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir.
The meeting began at 9pm and is still currently underway.
Speaking to reporters on arrival, Mohamad said the meeting was intended to resolve issues affecting the state, including the Menteri Besar's position.
"Malaysia is a constitutional country governed by laws. Everything must therefore be done properly.
"If the proper procedures are followed, I don't think there will be any issues. Follow the rules and don't take shortcuts," he said.
Mohamad said he hoped the political crisis in Negri Sembilan could be resolved as soon as possible.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Chased by bikers, Hilux driver claims he drove against traffic in panic
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Toyota Hilux driver who was caught driving against traffic along Jalan Raja Laut here early today claimed he panicked after being chased by a group of motorcyclists.
Federal Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department deputy chief Superintendent Suffian Abdullah said the incident occurred at 2.47am.
"Initial investigations found that the 33-year-old man was driving the Toyota Hilux against traffic from Jalan Sultan Ismail towards Jalan 1/64D.
"A group of motorcyclists then chased the vehicle, with several individuals believed to have struck it with their helmets," he said in a statement today.
Suffian said the driver was arrested to assist investigations under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
He said the man claimed he had panicked and lost control of the vehicle while attempting to escape the pursuing motorcyclists.
The driver was also suspected of hitting a motorcycle before skidding and crashing into a road divider.
"He sustained bruises to his face, body and hands.
"Alcohol and urine screening tests returned negative results," Suffian said.
Several videos showing a group of motorcyclists chasing and attacking a pickup truck had earlier gone viral on social media.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mamdani plan pushes closure of notorious New York jail to 2032
Article:
NEW YORK: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Friday released a plan to close the city's notorious Rikers Island jail complex by 2032 — five years past the original target date.
Long criticised for unsanitary and violent conditions, the facility, which opened in 1932, has counted John Lennon's killer Mark David Chapman, rapper Tupac Shakur and Sex Pistols musician Sid Vicious among its residents.
"For decades, New Yorkers have demanded a correctional system that is safe and humane," Mamdani said in a statement, adding that the plan would close Rikers, reduce pretrial detention and case delays, and invest US$146 million in programmes to keep people out of jail.
"We have a legal and moral obligation to close Rikers," the Democrat said.
Mamdani's predecessor, Bill de Blasio, had pledged to close Rikers Island by August 2027, but with less than a year left until that deadline, the four smaller jails intended to replace it were still under construction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: From palace walls to fabric: Perak unveils its signature batik
Article:
IPOH: A royal floral motif that has adorned Perak's palaces for generations is now being woven into the state's bid to establish a distinctive batik identity.
The Kelumpang Flower motif, inspired by traditional palace carvings, is the centrepiece of Batik Perak, which was officially launched by Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah today.
Also present were Raja Permaisuri of Perak Tuanku Zara Salim, Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and Media Prima Group chairman Datuk Seri Dr Syed Hussian Aljunid.
In his speech, Saarani said Batik Perak could evolve into a strong cultural and economic symbol for the state, creating new opportunities for local artisans while showcasing Perak's heritage internationally.
He said the Kelumpang Flower motif had deep roots in the state's royal heritage, featuring in palace carvings for generations.
Among the locations where it could be found were the entrance to the Balairung Seri at Istana Iskandariah in Kuala Kangsar and the Sultan Azlan Shah Gallery, formerly Istana Ulu.
"From the carvings adorning the palaces, the beauty of the Kelumpang Flower is now translated onto fabric, as though continuing an old story through a new work of art," he said.
Saarani said the Kelumpang Jari, scientifically known as Sterculia foetida, was chosen as the main motif for its distinctive finger-like leaves, purplish-green flowers and star-shaped fruit arrangement.
The initiative was spearheaded by Kraftangan Malaysia's Perak branch in February 2023, followed by a proposal to Perak Menteri Besar Incorporated (MB Inc) to extend the motif to various craft products, including batik, gold-thread embroidery and ceramics.
"In August 2024, the state executive council agreed to adopt the Kelumpang Flower as the official identity of Batik Perak, alongside the innovative use of clay in its production.
"Efforts were also undertaken to protect both elements through the Intellectual Property Corporation of Malaysia, ensuring that the authenticity of the identity developed would be preserved," he said.
Saarani said each piece of batik reflected the dedication, patience and skill of artisans who had spent years perfecting their craft.
Beyond preserving traditional skills, he said the industry continued to provide livelihoods and opportunities for younger generations to carry on the craft.
The state government, he added, had supported local artisans through Kraftangan Malaysia's Craft Community Development Project in Bagan Serai, Selama, Muallim, Tapah, Lenggong, Kuala Kangsar, Gerik and Kampung Gajah.
Batik Perak was also showcased at MAHA 2024 and MAHA 2026, with the Kelumpang Flower motif featured in craft demonstrations.
"The state government is also studying a proposal to make Batik Perak the official attire for state civil servants.
"This would give local craftsmanship wider recognition and make it a source of pride for the people of Perak," he said.
Saarani said the copyright registration application for the Perak State Motif design, Batik Kelumpang, submitted on April 16, 2025, was approved on May 19 that year.
He expressed confidence that Batik Perak would become a popular choice among Perakians, while expanding economic opportunities for local artisans.
"With the uniqueness of the Kelumpang Flower motif, I believe Batik Perak can become the preferred attire of the people of Perak, create wider livelihood opportunities for artisans and take the state's name onto the international stage," he said.

Title: Human Rights Tribunal in final stages, bill to give Suhakam reports teeth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A proposed Human Rights Tribunal to strengthen the enforcement of recommendations by the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) is in its final stages, with the enabling legislation expected to be tabled in Parliament soon.
Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran said the tribunal would ensure that Suhakam's findings and recommendations were acted upon without imposing hefty legal costs on the public.
"Other countries have a Human Rights Tribunal, and we are also at the final stage on this matter.
"We hope we have enough time, unless Parliament is dissolved earlier, to see it through and introduce the necessary legislation so that people can benefit from it.
"It is inexpensive and reasonable to maintain. If other countries can do it, why can't we?" he said in his keynote address at the Malaysia Legal Forum 2026 at the Asian International Arbitration Centre here today.
Kulasegaran said Suhakam had produced numerous reports over the years, but many had not received sufficient attention, including in Parliament.
"Over the years, I have noticed that they have submitted countless Human Rights Commission reports. Many of us do not even have time to look at them. We tell the office boy to put them in the car and take them to the office. We do not have time to read them.
"But many people are affected by these issues and want change. These reports are very important," he said.
He said discussions on Suhakam's reports had received greater attention under the current Madani government, which had allocated dedicated time in Parliament for their deliberation.
However, the absence of an enforcement mechanism remained a major obstacle, he said, adding that pursuing human rights cases through the conventional court system, from the High Court to the Federal Court, was costly and time-consuming for ordinary citizens.
On other legal reforms, Kulasegaran said proposals to separate the roles of the Attorney-General and Public Prosecutor, and to limit the Prime Minister's tenure to 10 years, were also at their final stages and expected to advance during the next parliamentary sitting.
"From what I know and from what I have gathered through internal discussions, I believe it will go through in the coming parliamentary session. That will be a great exercise.
"The other proposal is to limit the Prime Minister's term to 10 years. That, too, is at the final stage," he said.
Kulasegaran said the government was also considering a Mental Capacity Act to regulate the management and distribution of funds belonging to individuals who lacked the mental capacity to manage their own affairs.
He said the proposed law would establish a clearer legal framework and safeguards, including for compensation received by individuals or their families, drawing on Singapore's model.
"Like in Singapore, we understand that they have certain governance measures in place. We have had substantive discussions on this. The government is fully agreeable, and this is also in the pipeline and should be coming soon," he said.
He added that discussions on a proposed Charities Act were also at an advanced stage after three years of work.
Although Malaysia already had the Trustee Act, he said a dedicated law to regulate and govern charitable organisations was equally important.

Title: Negri exco shake-up: 7 assemblymen sign letters ahead of swearing-in
Article:

Title: Japan agrees to buy up to 8 mln barrels of Saudi crude to rebuild oil reserves
Article:
ISTANBUL: Japan has agreed to buy up to 8 million barrels of Saudi crude for its national petroleum reserve if market conditions are favourable, the two countries said Friday, Anadolu Ajansi reported, citing Saudi Press Agency.
The agreement also expands the storage capacity available to Saudi Arabia in Japan.
The kingdom, which already has access to 8 million barrels of capacity, will gain temporary use of storage for 16 million barrels, according to a joint statement carried by the Saudi Press Agency.
Saudi Arabia has already begun replenishing crude stocks at storage facilities in Japan, the statement said.
Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman and Japan's Economy, Trade and Industry Minister Ryosei Akazawa reached the agreement during a virtual meeting.
The ministers reaffirmed their commitment to cooperation on long-term energy security.
Japan is among the oil importers that drew on emergency reserves when the US-Iran war disrupted shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. Oil flows from Gulf producers have since recovered to near prewar levels, giving buyers an opportunity to rebuild depleted stockpiles.
For Saudi Arabia, storing crude in Japan puts supplies closer to Asian customers and makes them available if shipping through Hormuz is disrupted again.
Saudi Aramco Chief Executive Amin Nasser said last month that the kingdom had held talks with foreign governments about giving the state-owned oil company access to their strategic storage facilities.

Title: 'Every year my house floods': Rantau Panjang braces for rising waters
Article:
KOTA BARU: Residents in Rantau Panjang are keeping a close watch on Sungai Golok as its rising water level fuels fears of flooding, particularly if rain continues.
A Bernama survey found that intermittent rain and unpredictable weather had prompted residents to monitor the river closely, with heavy rainfall in nearby Narathiwat, Thailand, adding to their concerns.
Although the river has yet to overflow into residential areas, those living along its banks are taking precautions and preparing for possible flooding.
Resident Nik Ahmad Nik Ismail, 40, said the rising water level had prompted him to check the river more frequently.
"It is better to remain vigilant and keep abreast of the latest developments," he told Bernama today.
Another resident, Wan Che Zainab Wan Che Mat, 55, said heavy rain in Narathiwat had heightened anxiety among those living near the river.
Having experienced floods almost every year, she said she had become accustomed to her home being inundated but remained uneasy whenever the water level rose.
"My house is flooded almost every year. I am used to it, but I still feel worried whenever I see the river's water level rising," she said.
Yesterday, one of four river monitoring stations in Kelantan recorded a reading above the alert level as of 10.45pm.
Data from the Department of Irrigation and Drainage's Public Infobanjir portal showed that Sungai Golok at Rantau Panjang, Pasir Mas, had reached 7.18 metres, exceeding the alert level of 7 metres.

Title: ITMAX to raise RM1bil from sukuk issuances
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: ITMAX System Bhd has established two Islamic financing programmes with a combined limit of RM1 billion to fund its business operations and refinance existing borrowings.
The smart city solutions provider said its wholly owned ITMAX Capital Sdn Bhd lodged the required documents with the Securities Commission for an Islamic medium-term notes (IMTN) programme and an Islamic commercial papers (ICP) programme.
The IMTN has a perpetual limit, while the ICP has a tenure of up to seven years.
Individual issuances under the IMTN will have tenures of one year, while those under the ICP will range from one to 12 months.
ITMAX said the sukuk wakalah programmes are unsecured, although individual series or tranches may be issued on either an unsecured or secured basis.
Proceeds will be used for the group's Shariah-compliant general business, commodity purchases, refinancing of existing Shariah-compliant or conventional obligations, and future Shariah-compliant financing.
AmInvestment Bank Bhd is the principal adviser, lead arranger, lead manager, facility agent and security agent, while AmBank Islamic Bhd is the Islamic adviser.

Title: Three held as police uncover RM1.27mil stash of health and beauty products
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police detained three men and seized health, cosmetic and food products worth RM1.27 million in a raid on a logistics premises in Banting, Selangor, yesterday.
The operation, codenamed Op Taring Dosej, was conducted at 12.10pm by the Bukit Aman Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Intelligence Investigation, under the Internal Security and Public Order Department, with several enforcement agencies.
Bukit Aman Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Intelligence Investigation commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said those detained were a local man believed to be the company owner and two Bangladeshi employees.
Checks uncovered 1,044 boxes of health and cosmetic products, 1,300 bottles of supplements and health products, 38 boxes of tremella soup products, 65 boxes of coenzyme Q10 products, as well as various tea-based food and beverage products and snacks.
"All seized items have been handed over to the respective enforcement agencies for further action and investigation under their respective jurisdictions," he said in a statement today.
The total value of the seizure was estimated at RM1.27 million, with the Health Ministry accounting for the bulk at RM1.26 million. The Kuala Langat District Health Office seized items worth RM5,167, while the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry accounted for RM4,745.
The operation also involved the Selangor Health Ministry's Pharmacy Division, the Customs Department's Klang branch, the Kuala Langat District Health Office, the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry and the Kuala Langat Municipal Council (MPKL).
The district health office issued two compounds totalling RM4,500, while MPKL issued another two amounting to RM2,000.
The case is being investigated under the Immigration Act 1959/63, Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984, Trade Descriptions Act 2011, Food Act 1983 and related regulations.
Zaki said police would continue to intensify enforcement and intelligence operations to curb smuggling and the distribution of illicit goods.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Firefighters save woman threatening to jump into sea
Article:

Title: Evidence in former Petronas manager's case met international standards, court told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Evidence stored by CyberSecurity Malaysia in the case involving former Petronas manager Mohd Khairul Akmal fully complied with international standards set by the American Society of Crime Laboratory Directors (ASCLD), the Sessions Court heard today.
CyberSecurity Malaysia Senior Digital Forensic Analyst Abdul Wafi Abdul Rahman, 38, said the agency's internal chain-of-custody procedures applied only within its forensic laboratory.
"The internal chain of custody applies only within the laboratory, involving the recipient, storekeeper and analyst. It does not include police investigating officers. These procedures apply only to internal processes after the exhibits have been handed over to us," he said.
The seventh prosecution witness was responding to questions during re-examination by Deputy Public Prosecutor Noor Syafina Mohd Radzuan in the trial of Mohd Khairul Akmal, who is charged with attempting to disclose Petronas' business report and financial structure to Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros) on June 8, 2024.
Yesterday, Abdul Wafi told the court that he had examined a laptop belonging to the accused, two mobile phones and a USB drive between Dec 19, 2024 and Jan 24, 2025 to determine whether they contained any information related to the alleged attempt to transmit the documents.
Meanwhile, Abdul Wafi said he did not trace the location of Mohd Khairul Akmal's laptop, which was allegedly used in an attempt to send confidential information on the national oil company's business and financial structure to Petros, as this was the responsibility of telecommunications companies.
"It is not the responsibility of CyberSecurity Malaysia or myself to trace the location of the perpetrator or the whereabouts of the exhibits within the country, as that is the responsibility of telecommunications companies," he said.
He also said he did not analyse internet connection records in the laptop's event log when preparing the digital forensic report, as this was not within the scope of the investigation requested by the investigating officer.
"If the laptop had used an internet hotspot registered under another individual's name on the date of the incident, the connection activity should have been recorded in the log," he said.
Mohd Khairul Akmal, 41, is charged with attempting to disclose a document entitled 'Q1 2024 Upstream Business Performance Operational & Financial' to Petros, which he had obtained in the course of his duties as Petronas Business Unit Performance Manager, at a condominium unit in Jalan Pinang here, between 3.19 pm and 3.21 pm on June 8, 2024.
The charge is framed under Section 203A(1) of the Penal Code, read together with Section 511 of the same Code. Upon conviction, Section 203A(1) provides for a maximum fine of RM1 million or imprisonment for up to one year, while Section 511 provides for imprisonment of up to half the maximum term prescribed under Section 203A(1).
The trial before Judge Mazuliana Abdul Rashid continues on Feb 9 next year. – BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'They were inseparable': Siblings, 13 and 10, die in house fire [WATCH]
Article:
TAWAU: "Muhammad Nor Fazryn always looked after his younger sister, wherever he went. They were inseparable. Sadly, neither made it out of the fire."
That was the heartbreaking account of their aunt, Noreen Malvine, 37, following the deaths of the siblings, aged 13 and 10, in a
house fire
at Taman Ria 11 here early today.
Noreen said her nephew, Muhammad Nor Fazryn Norman, and his 10-year-old sister, Nurailin Nathania, who was autistic, were trapped in an upstairs room of their double-storey terrace house when the fire broke out about 6am.
The room's windows were fitted with security grilles, leaving the children with no way out, she said.
Describing Nor Fazryn as an intelligent and protective older brother, Noreen said he was particularly attentive to Nurailin, whom he rarely left alone.
She said the children's mother, Nor Fazrina Edayu Faisal, had tried desperately to reach them but was eventually forced to escape through a second-floor bedroom window with her three other children when the roof collapsed.
"My sister-in-law fractured her spine when she jumped, while one of her children developed asthma after inhaling the thick smoke," she said.
Noreen said she took the injured mother and her three children to Tawau Hospital, while other family members continued searching for the two missing siblings.
The family later received confirmation that both children had been found dead.
She said Nor Fazrina Edayu was in stable condition but remained hospitalised for treatment. Her husband was making his way back to Tawau from his workplace in Kota Kinabalu.
Tawau Fire and Rescue Station chief Jemishin Ujin said the department received an emergency call at 6.13am and arrived at the scene nine minutes later.
"Upon arrival, we estimated that 70 per cent of the double-storey terrace house was already engulfed in flames.
"Firefighters used water from the fire engine's tank and a fire hydrant to put out the blaze before finding the two children dead in a room," he said.
The cause of the fire is still under investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MN Holdings lands record RM1.12bil solar deal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MN Holdings Bhd has secured its biggest contract to date, a RM1.12 billion deal as part of a consortium to build two large-scale solar farms in Kemaman, Terengganu.
The engineering and construction contract also marks the group's first entry into the large-scale solar segment.
MN Holdings will lead the consortium in delivering the two solar facilities, which have contracted export capacities of 250 megawatts alternating current (MWac) and 150MWac respectively, bringing their combined capacity to 400MWac.
The project was awarded by RE Kemaman Sdn Bhd and RE Kemaman II Sdn Bhd under the LSS Petra 5+ programme.
The scope covers the integrated design, engineering, procurement, construction, testing and commissioning of the facilities, including associated interconnection infrastructure and related works.
Work will begin upon receipt of the notice to proceed or limited notice to proceed from the clients, with completion targeted by 2028.
MN Holdings said it will pursue further opportunities in renewable energy projects, leveraging its existing technical capabilities and project execution experience.
Beyond its core engineering and construction business, the company is also exploring strategic equity investments in renewable energy projects.
"We believe this approach will support a more diversified earnings base and strengthen the company's long-term growth prospects," it said.
